newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: JCI says almost all gold miners on strike.
newsitem.headline: JCI says almost all gold miners on strike.

text.p: JCI Ltd said on Monday most of its workers had heeded a one-day strike called by South Africa's biggest labour federation, the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu).
"We have not quite 100 percent, but a majority stay-away at the three gold mines," spokesman Craig Lawrence told Reuters.
Lawrence said there was no substantial output from the H.J. Joel Gold Mining Co Ltd, Randfontein Estates Gold Mining Co Ltd and Western Areas Gold Mining Co Ltd mines.
"It's a majority stay-away so production is going to be very significantly affected," he added.
Lawrence said the action had started with Sunday's night shift failing to report for work at the gold mines.
Cosatu has mobilised for a one-day strike to protest the Basic Conditions of Employment Bill which has already passed through Cabinet and is expected to be tabled before parliament soon.
It is demanding a 40-hour working week, six months maternity leave and double pay for Sunday work.
